thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: multi-GPU NCCL communicator timeouts detected in cluster gpudev-4 during ongoing TP4 training jobs. Rollup: OOMs/CUDA XIDs + ncclCommTimeout across 3 nodes. Links: https://redwood.in/alerts/2765432100 and trace: https://ops.redwood/trace/2765432100

alice-nguyen: saw the pager, I'm on it. Starting triage — which jobs are impacted?

samir-ops: affected: job-rl-42 (customer A), job-llm-finetune-7 (internal), job-reco-3 (customer B). All are tensor-parallel (TP=4) on p4d-24xlarge-style hosts.

hannah-runtime: quick summary from runtime metrics: memory usage spikes followed by CUDA XID 79 on GPU 2 in node gpudev-4-12, then nccl communicator errors on all ranks. KV cache looks intact but comms are stalling.

devon-sre: can we drain gpudev-4-12 and cordon it to stop new allocations? I'll prepare a taint.

alice-nguyen: yes please. samir, can you get us logs from the container on gpudev-4-12? run `sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 500` and paste the NCCL lines.

samir-ops: grabbing logs now. Pasting relevant tail:```
[2026-03-15T10:12:09Z] runtime: GPU 2 CUDA ERROR: XID 79, process 32145
[2026-03-15T10:12:09Z] runtime: ncclCommInitRank failed: Unrecoverable error (NCCL_INTERNAL_ERROR)
[2026-03-15T10:12:10Z] runtime: allreduce failed, timeout waiting on rank 2
[2026-03-15T10:12:10Z] runtime: process 32145 killed (oom?)
[2026-03-15T10:12:12Z] runtime: reconnect attempts from remaining ranks
```

samir-ops: nodes gpudev-4-12, gpudev-4-13, gpudev-4-14 show correlated GPU driver resets. Looks like a software path causing recurrent XID 79s.

hannah-runtime: that matches our kernel-driver telemetry spikes — PCIe error counters incremented right before XID. Could be thermal or driver bug. But immediate mitigation: we should fallback the TP4 jobs to TP2 (reduce degree) or re-route to single-GPU variants where possible. That avoids NCCL collectives.

jason-eng: for customer-facing jobs we prefer non-disruptive route: spin up compatible single-GPU model variant and redirect traffic. For training, we may need to pause and migrate checkpoints.

devon-sre: I'm cordoning gpudev-4-12 now and draining active pods: `kubectl cordon gpudev-4-12 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpudev-4-12`.

alice-nguyen: I'm notifying customers A and B via CS. @maya-customer-success can you post an ETA note and request logs/checkpoints?

maya-customer-success: on it, pinged both with current status and asked for permission to failover to single-GPU serving replicas; waiting on acks.

hannah-runtime: meanwhile, I'll flip the NCCL fallback policy for the cluster to `allow_fallback:true` so runtime will try non-collective execution paths when communicator init fails. Patching config now.

hannah-runtime: patch applied: `/etc/redwood/runtime/config.yaml` diff snippet:```
- nccl: {strict: true, timeout_ms: 120000} 
+ nccl: {strict: false, timeout_ms: 60000, allow_fallback: true} 
```

hannah-runtime: restarting runtime on gpudev-4-13/14 to pick up config. `systemctl restart redwood-runtime`

samir-ops: restarted services. Observing job-llm-finetune-7 re-establishing with fallback path — logs show new path using `distributed=allreduce_emulation` instead of native NCCL.

alice-nguyen: are we seeing reduced errors? telemetry?

hannah-runtime: error rate dropped by ~80% across the cluster. No new XID 79s in the last 45s, but we still have degraded throughput and higher latency for those jobs.

devon-sre: since we cordoned gpudev-4-12, can we reprovision a replacement host for customers that need capacity? I'll open a spare node from the pool. `provision-host --flavor p4d-24 --pool gpudev-4`

samir-ops: spare host launching as gpudev-4-18. I'll add it to the autoscaling group and let the scheduler place evacuated pods.

jason-eng: for the training jobs we should schedule a maintenance window to restart with newer driver; recommend NVIDIA driver 525. Plus set `GDS_ENABLE=false` for now if used.

hannah-runtime: capturing all relevant traces and creating a condensed incident log. Creating ticket: INC-2765432100 with root cause hypothesis "driver/XID-induced GPU reset causing NCCL communicator init failures; exacerbated by TP4 allreduce sensitivity".

alice-nguyen: passing to next on-call in 30m. @pager-duty-bot please handoff to night on-call at 2765433900. Include steps taken, current status, and action items.

pager-duty-bot: Handoff scheduled to night-oncall at 2765433900. Included summary and links.

maya-customer-success: customers A/B accepted the single-GPU fallback for serving; customer A requested a follow-up postmortem and ETA for driver patch.

hannah-runtime: action items for follow-up: 1) reproduce XID 79 with host-level stress tests, 2) test driver upgrade on staging pool, 3) add runtime guardrails to reduce TP degree automatically when repeated NCCL timeouts detected, 4) customer postmortems.

devon-sre: logging those as tasks on INC-2765432100 and assigning owners. I'm leaving notes for night on-call to monitor XID counts and to promote staging driver if clean.

alice-nguyen: Thanks everyone. Moving to monitoring-only. If anything spikes again, reactivate pager. :thumbsup:

pager-duty-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status changed to MONITORING.

samir-ops: final note — we captured core dump from process 32145 and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-2765432100/dumps/32145.core for offline analysis.

jason-eng: will pick that up tomorrow for deep dive. For now, mitigations stand.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging but remains on MONITORING."
